supersedes: docs/art/run-card-family-prompts-v2.json (left intact as the record of what shipped)
note: The 69 cards dealable under DEFAULT_RUN_RULES (cardSpan 2), each authored across the three layers of the contract. One illustration per CARD, retiring the (footprint, roster) family collapse of ADR-0520 for this deck.

layerStatus.voice: proposed — the register the fifteen Kings already print. Unaffected by slate sign-off.
layerStatus.cast: proposed — the Cessolis reading. Unaffected by slate sign-off.
layerStatus.act: SUPERSEDED IN PART. These act lines were authored during the single-war pass (Orléans, 12 Oct 1428 – 8 May 1429) which the owner replaced with the king-rooted structure. The MOMENTS remain valid and reusable; the days are reassigned to King worlds once the slate is signed off. See rollup in run-king-slate-v3.json for target counts per world.

rules.priceIsNotAnInput: A card’s gold contributes nothing to its picture.
rules.noArrangementField: The footprint may be echoed by a composition that can do it without posing anybody, and is dropped the instant it costs the scene. It is never the subject.
rules.seatingSelectsTheMoment: Cards sharing a footprint and roster differ by which instant of the shared act they hold, not by geometry.
rules.attestedFlag: act.attested marks a documented event. Unmarked days are authored moments inside a documented world — true in kind, not claims about a date. The act never reaches the card face either way.

current.name: Wandering Preacher
current.flavor: The sanctuary was gone. The lesson continued beside the road.

voice.name: One chaplain, retained, 6d
voice.flavor: Allowed by the indenture to say mass and keep the roll. He does both badly.
voice.moment: The indenture signed at a plank table, the wax still soft, his other hand already on the muster book.

cast.name: The Judge Without a Bench
cast.reading: He was appointed to hear the assize at Michaelmas. The hall had been let to a wool merchant.
cast.moment: He sets his roll on a milestone and begins reading the charge aloud to nobody, because the reading is required.

act.detail: The suburbs came down so the English would have nothing to stand in. The canons carried out what they could.
act.moment: A canon walking away from his own church with the reliquary, as behind him the townsmen swing the first beam out of the roof.

current.name: Errant Rider
current.flavor: Every road was marked urgent. None said where it led.

voice.name: Retained: one man-at-arms, 12d
voice.flavor: Attested at the array. Horse valued at forty livres, so the crown owes for it if it dies.
voice.moment: The clerk chalking the horse's value onto its own flank while the rider holds its head.

cast.name: The Chevalier Sworn
cast.reading: He swore to defend the church, the widow and the orphan. The oath does not say in which order.
cast.moment: The instant after the oath: his hand still on the relic, the priest already turning away, the horse brought up behind him.

act.detail: One rider went out before the ring closed. Everything the town later hoped for went out with him.
act.moment: Looking back at the walls from the last rise where they are still visible, and deciding not to stop.

current.name: The Volunteer
current.flavor: The frost came in June. By August, the road had found him.

voice.name: Retained: one foot archer, 3d
voice.flavor: Made his mark. Cannot be paid until the second muster, which is forty days off.
voice.moment: His mark going onto the roll — a cross, drawn slowly, the clerk's pen turned round for him.

cast.name: The Labourer Called Up
cast.reading: Cessolis gives the first pawn a spade in one hand and a rod in the other. The array took the rod.
cast.moment: Handing the spade over a low wall to his wife, keeping the rod, which from this morning is a weapon.

act.detail: The first of the burned suburbs. The men who pulled them down had lived in them.
act.moment: Putting a torch to his own thatch at arm's length, not looking at it.

current.name: Regal Serenity
current.flavor: She watched the empty court until ceremony became weather.

voice.name: Under the banner of a banneret, 4s
voice.flavor: The whole roll is written beneath one name. She is the reason the rest of it can be paid.
voice.moment: The banner going up over the muster field: the instant the cloth takes the wind and men start walking toward it.

cast.name: The Intercession
cast.reading: Cessolis gives the queen mercy, and mercy is a thing done in public or not at all.
cast.moment: She has stepped between the sentence and the man, and the court has not yet decided what to do about it.

act.detail: She entered at eight in the evening carrying her standard, and the town did not sleep.
act.moment: Torchlight catching the standard the moment it clears the gate arch — the crowd's faces turn before she does.

current.name: The Watchtower
current.flavor: From the tower, every road led away.

voice.name: One master mason, 8d, and his tools
voice.flavor: Entered as a man-at-arms because the roll has no line for him. He is worth three.
voice.moment: Chalking the line of the new boulevard onto trampled ground while the labourers wait with their baskets.

cast.name: The King's Legate
cast.reading: The rook is not a tower. Cessolis makes him the king's vicar, sent out with the king's authority in a satchel.
cast.moment: Holding the sealed commission up to a closed gate, while the men on the gate read it slowly.

act.detail: They took the bridge fort two days after the wound that killed Salisbury. It was worth more than he was.
act.moment: English soldiers on the captured tower roof, turned back down the bridge toward the town, which is now the only thing left.

current.name: Matins and Vespers
current.flavor: Matins stood before Vespers because the roof admitted only one.

voice.name: Two chaplains, 6d each, forty days
voice.flavor: One for the retinue, one for the sick. Both entered on the same line to save parchment.
voice.moment: Two men signing the same page in turn, the second waiting with his hand already out for the pen.

cast.name: Two Judges, One Bench
cast.reading: The assize was to be heard by two. The bench seats two, in order, and they had not agreed the order.
cast.moment: Both men reaching the bench at the same moment, and neither sitting.

act.detail: Both sides kept the day. The English asked for music and the town sent its minstrels across.
act.moment: The minstrels walking out onto open ground between the bastille and the wall, instruments up, nobody armed.

current.name: Pilgrim's Shelter
current.flavor: The lamp went first. The sermon followed where it could.

voice.name: One archer, one chaplain
voice.flavor: The archer is paid 6d and the chaplain 6d, which the archer has noticed.
voice.moment: The pay table: two hands out, one coin counted into each, the same count.

cast.name: The Clerk and His Judge
cast.reading: The third pawn is the notary: shears in one hand, pen in the other. He walks in front because he carries the writ.
cast.moment: The writ held out ahead at arm's length, the judge a pace behind, both walking into a yard that has gone quiet.

act.detail: The town walked its relics round the inside of the walls. It had nothing else to put on them.
act.moment: The head of the procession reaching the corner where the wall is thinnest, and the boy with the cross looking up at it.

current.name: Squire's Shelter
current.flavor: The rider waited behind the only order that had arrived.

voice.name: A lance: one man-at-arms, one page
voice.flavor: The lance is three men. This one is two, and the clerk has written 'wanting one'.
voice.moment: The pen pausing over the gap in the line where the third man should be standing.

cast.name: The Ribald Sent Ahead
cast.reading: The eighth pawn is the messenger and the dice-player. He goes first because he is the fastest and the most expendable.
cast.moment: Already twenty paces up the lane and turning to signal, while the rider is still holding the horse.

act.detail: A scout and a rider went to see whether the English were where they were said to be. They were.
act.moment: The scout dropping flat behind a hedge; the rider, still mounted and still visible, understanding a heartbeat later.

current.name: The Last Attendant
current.flavor: One attendant remained after the court learned to empty itself.

voice.name: The banneret and her page, final tally
voice.flavor: The roll closes here. Four shillings and threepence, and the campaign is over.
voice.moment: The last two lines of the roll being ruled off, coin still loose on the table.

cast.name: The Last Attendant
cast.reading: Mercy needs somebody to carry it. By the end she had one man, and he was the taverner's son.
cast.moment: He holds the door of an emptied hall open for her, and there is nobody behind her.

act.detail: Hit in the shoulder at noon, back at dusk. The fort fell within the hour.
act.moment: Her standard going up against the boulevard wall with one soldier beside her, the ladders behind them still empty.

current.name: Gatekeeper's Charge
current.flavor: The gatekeeper put one name between the wall and morning.

voice.name: One archer, to the master mason
voice.flavor: Assigned to carry, not to shoot. Paid as an archer, worked as a labourer, complained in writing.
voice.moment: Setting his bow down against the scaffold to pick up a hod.

cast.name: The Guard and the Legate
cast.reading: The seventh pawn keeps the gate and takes the toll. The legate has a commission, which is not a toll.
cast.moment: The guard's arm across the gate and the legate's seal held up beside it, each waiting for the other to move first.

act.detail: The English finished it in the rain. From then the river road was theirs.
act.moment: A sentry stepping up onto the new wall-walk for the first time, boots in wet mortar.

current.name: The Twin Keeps
current.flavor: One keep watched the road. The other watched the first.

voice.name: Two lieutenants, garrison, 12d each
voice.flavor: One holds the gate, one holds the bridge. Both are paid to be elsewhere if it goes wrong.
voice.moment: Two men handed the same written order at the same table, reading it in opposite directions.

cast.name: Two Commissions, One Road
cast.reading: Both men carried the king's authority. The road was wide enough for one of them at a time.
cast.moment: Two sealed commissions held up side by side at the same barrier, and the barrier-keeper reading both.

act.detail: They formed up in the field, waited to be attacked, were not, and marched away.
act.moment: The English lines standing empty at first light with the fires still smoking, seen from the town wall.

current.name: Thundering Lances
current.flavor: Neither rider yielded the width of the road.

voice.name: Two men-at-arms, 12d, one horse valued
voice.flavor: The second horse was never appraised, so the crown owes nothing for it. He rode it anyway.
voice.moment: Two riders at the appraisal: one horse chalked, the other's flank clean.

cast.name: Two Chevaliers Abreast
cast.reading: Cessolis says the knight must be tested before he is trusted. Neither had been, and each said so of the other.
cast.moment: Two horses shoulder to shoulder in a lane too narrow for it, both riders looking straight ahead.

act.line: Out of the Renart Gate, 5 December
act.detail: Two captains rode out at dawn to see what could be taken. They came back with cattle.
act.moment: Coming back through the gate at a walk, driving stolen cattle, and nobody cheering yet.

current.name: Two Good Boots
current.flavor: The road kept both pairs of boots, and returned neither name.

voice.name: Two foot archers, 3d, forty days
voice.flavor: Brothers. Entered together, and the second is a head shorter than the roll allows.
voice.moment: Both measured against the same marked post, the shorter one on his toes.

cast.name: The Smith and the Labourer
cast.reading: Second pawn and first: the hammer and the spade. Between them they can make everything the war needs and none of what it takes.
cast.moment: The smith handing a mended billhook back across the anvil; the labourer already turning to go.

act.line: The Levy of the Quarters, 14 October
act.detail: Each quarter of the town found its men. The rolls were read out in the street.
act.moment: Two men stepping out of a crowd at the reading of their names, at the moment the crowd closes behind them.

current.name: Cloister and Keep
current.flavor: The cloister was sold. The keep remained employed.

voice.name: One lieutenant, one clerk of the muster
voice.flavor: The clerk counts what the lieutenant commands. Neither trusts the other's arithmetic.
voice.moment: The tally-stick being split between them, each taking half.

cast.name: The Legate and the Judge
cast.reading: One carried the king's authority, the other the law's. They agreed the case was urgent and agreed on nothing else.
cast.moment: Two men reading one document at one table from opposite sides, neither letting go of it.

act.detail: The convoy was salted fish for Lent. They laagered the carts, and the French rode at them anyway.
act.moment: The instant the first French horse reaches the barricade of herring barrels and finds that it does not give.

current.name: Sword and Censer
current.flavor: The blade guarded the road; the censer remembered the room.

voice.name: One chaplain, one man-at-arms
voice.flavor: The chaplain attests the man-at-arms is who he says. The clerk has no way to check either.
voice.moment: The chaplain's hand on the man's shoulder at the attestation, the clerk not looking up.

cast.name: The Judge and the Chevalier
cast.reading: The alphin decides who is guilty and the knight decides what happens next. Cessolis is careful to keep them apart.
cast.moment: The judge finishing a sentence aloud while behind him the knight is already loosening a strap.

act.detail: The bell was rung each evening and both armies stopped for it. Then it stopped being rung.
act.moment: A rider halted in the open at the sound, hat off, the bell tower lit behind him and the bastilles dark.

current.name: Castellan's Sally
current.flavor: At dawn the castellan rode through an abbey with no brothers.

voice.name: Lieutenant and escort, to Blois
voice.flavor: Ordered out and back. Paid for eight days, took eleven, argued for three.
voice.moment: Two riders handed a sealed bag at a gate, one signing for it.

cast.name: The Legate Escorted
cast.reading: The commission travels no faster than the man guarding it, and the man guarding it is not paid to hurry.
cast.moment: The legate reining in because the escort has stopped, and the escort pointing at something out of frame.

act.detail: They rode out to meet the convoy and met it too late, in the open, in the wrong order.
act.moment: The Orléans horse arriving on the field at the moment the Scots are already committed on foot ahead of them.

current.name: Council in the Corner
current.flavor: Three doctrines in one corner, and the corner not large enough for one.

voice.name: Three chaplains, one retinue
voice.flavor: Two too many for a company this size. The third is somebody's brother.
voice.moment: Three men in a line at the pay table and one purse being opened.

cast.name: The Bench of Three
cast.reading: Three judges make a quorum. A quorum makes a decision, which is what nobody in the room wanted.
cast.moment: The instant the third judge sits down — because until he sat, there was no court.

act.detail: Before she was allowed near the town, three weeks of churchmen asked questions and wrote the answers down.
act.moment: Three clerics at a table, one writing; she is standing, and the writer has stopped.

current.name: Charger at the Bend
current.flavor: The charger took the bend and the two offices arrived by the inside.

voice.name: Two chaplains and their escort
voice.flavor: Carried the retinue's accounts to Rouen. The escort is charged at 12d and worth it.
voice.moment: The saddlebag of accounts being roped shut while the two clerics watch.

cast.name: The Escort of the Assize
cast.reading: Two judges to hear it, one knight to get them there. The knight was told the road was safe.
cast.moment: The horse shying at the bend; both judges' hands go out to the cart rail at the same instant.

act.line: The Churchmen Go to Chinon, 6 March
act.detail: Two clerics and one rider went to ask whether the king would receive her. The rider did the deciding.
act.moment: The rider halting the party at a crossroads and pointing down the road they were not told to take.

current.name: Rider Above the Chapter
current.flavor: The rider held the high side while the chapter argued the low one.

voice.name: Escort refused leave
voice.flavor: The chaplains asked to ride on ahead. The escort's orders say together, and he can read.
voice.moment: The escort holding the lead mule's bridle while a chaplain gestures up the road.

cast.name: The Chapter Overruled
cast.reading: The bench had reached its finding. The knight had reached the door first.
cast.moment: The knight in the doorway with the light behind him; the two judges have stopped mid-sentence.

act.line: Turned Back on the Chinon Road, 8 March
act.detail: They were sent to negotiate and came back having been told there was nothing to negotiate.
act.moment: The rider putting his horse across the road, and the two clerics reining up short of it.

current.name: Two Offices, One Charger
current.flavor: Two offices, one horse, and a road that would take only one of them.

voice.name: One horse, two claims
voice.flavor: Both chaplains have written to the captain about the same animal. Neither mentions the other.
voice.moment: Two written claims on one table, the horse visible through the door behind them.

cast.name: One Horse Between Two Courts
cast.reading: The court that gets the horse hears its case first. Both courts knew it.
cast.moment: One horse led out of a stable, and two judges arriving at the door from opposite sides.

act.line: The Road Is Only Wide Enough, 10 March
act.detail: Two clerics, one escort, one road, and news arriving from both ends of it at once.
act.moment: Two clerics facing opposite ways on the same road while the rider between them reads a letter.

current.name: Chaplain at the Bend
current.flavor: He blessed them at the turning, which was as far as he was going.

voice.name: Two men-at-arms and a chaplain
voice.flavor: The chaplain is entered at 6d and the horses at forty livres each. The roll knows what it values.
voice.moment: Two horses being appraised while the chaplain waits with nothing to be appraised.

cast.name: The Judge Between Two Lances
cast.reading: The alphin was sent to keep peace between them. He rode in the middle, which is where he was safest.
cast.moment: Both riders have turned in the saddle to look at each other past him, and he is looking straight ahead.

act.detail: The relief column formed up with the priests at the front and the captains behind, which the captains disliked.
act.moment: The column stepping off with the clergy leading, two captains sitting their horses at the roadside, not moving yet.

current.name: Office Above Two Lances
current.flavor: The office watched from above while both horses took the corner badly.

voice.name: Confession before the array
voice.flavor: Ordered by the captain. Attendance recorded, which is the point of it.
voice.moment: The chaplain marking names in a book while two riders wait, dismounted, holding their own reins.

cast.name: The Assize Above the Yard
cast.reading: He read the finding from the gallery, because the yard below had already made up its mind.
cast.moment: The judge at the rail with the roll open; below him two riders have stopped their horses to listen.

act.line: The Sermon Before the Column, 27 April
act.detail: He preached against swearing and looting to men recruited on the promise of both.
act.moment: The moment he names the penalty, and one of the two riders in front of him looks at the other.

current.name: Two Lances, One Chaplain
current.flavor: Two horses and one chaplain, and the chaplain kept the count.

voice.name: Second muster, two absent
voice.flavor: Both entered, both attested, both gone. The chaplain has written 'not found'.
voice.moment: Two blank spaces in a line of standing men, and the pen resting on the gap.

cast.name: The Count Kept by the Chaplain
cast.reading: Two knights went out. The chaplain's task was to write down how many came back.
cast.moment: The chaplain at the gate with the book open, watching the road, one rider visible on it.

act.detail: They came back with fewer than they took, and the count was made at the gate before anyone was let through.
act.moment: The book open on the gate ledge, a wet thumb holding the page, the first horses arriving.

current.name: Gallop at the Turning
current.flavor: They took the turning at speed. Two of the three came out of it.

voice.name: Three men-at-arms, one lance short
voice.flavor: A full lance is three. Three men-at-arms is not a lance, it is an expense.
voice.moment: Three appraised horses together and one clerk totalling a column he does not like.

cast.name: Three Sworn, One Road
cast.reading: Cessolis says a knight is made by the test and not by the oath. This was the test.
cast.moment: Three horses entering a bend abreast where there is room for two.

act.detail: The first fort taken. It went in an hour, and it decided that the rest could go too.
act.moment: The ladder topping the palisade at Saint-Loup with the men behind it still on the ground.

current.name: Two Offices at the Bend
current.flavor: Both offices took the bend. Neither conceded the inside.

voice.name: One archer to two chaplains
voice.flavor: Detailed to carry their gear. Paid 6d, carries sixty pounds, mentioned in no account.
voice.moment: Taking a second bundle onto an already-loaded back.

cast.name: The Notary Between Two Judges
cast.reading: The third pawn carries the pen. Both benches wanted the pen to write their version.
cast.moment: The clerk with the pen still wet, looking from one judge to the other, having written nothing.

act.detail: The bread was weighed by the church and issued by the church, and the weight went down in January.
act.moment: The scale pan settling at the new weight, the two churchmen watching it, the townsman's hands already out.

current.name: Chapter in the Corner
current.flavor: The chapter met in a corner because the hall had been requisitioned.

voice.name: Muster held in a granary
voice.flavor: No hall available. The roll was called between the sacks and the tally is grain-dusted.
voice.moment: The roll being called in a granary, the clerk's page grey with dust.

cast.name: The Chapter in a Borrowed Room
cast.reading: The hall had been requisitioned for grain. The court met in the corner it was given.
cast.moment: Two judges and a clerk at a small table with sacks stacked to the ceiling behind them.

act.detail: They stored grain where they had met for two hundred years, and held the meeting anyway.
act.moment: The meeting held standing between grain sacks, one man holding the roll up to a high window for light.

current.name: The Cornered Diocese
current.flavor: The diocese fit in a corner by then, and still argued about the seating.

voice.name: Two chaplains, one servant
voice.flavor: The servant is not on the roll. He is fed from the chaplains' allowance, which they resent.
voice.moment: Two men eating at a table and a third standing with the plate he carried in.

cast.name: The Diocese in One Corner
cast.reading: Everything the office still governed fit in the corner of a room, and they argued about the seating.
cast.moment: Two judges taking chairs at a table set for eight; the clerk is still deciding where to stand.

act.line: What Was Left of the See, 20 January
act.detail: The bishop was at Rome. What remained of his court was two canons and a boy with the keys.
act.moment: A boy handing a ring of keys to two canons in an empty vestry.

current.name: Cloister Beside the Keep
current.flavor: The cloister stood beside the keep and paid for the privilege in stone.

voice.name: One archer, one chaplain, one lieutenant
voice.flavor: The smallest complete sub-retinue on the roll, and the cheapest, which is why it exists.
voice.moment: A bracket being drawn round three names to make them one unit.

cast.name: The Court Beside the Commission
cast.reading: The judge had jurisdiction and the legate had the seal, and the man between them had the keys.
cast.moment: The gatekeeper holding the keys up between two men who are both reaching for them.

act.line: The Town Council Meets the Bastard, 25 April
act.detail: The town paid for the defence and wanted to be told how. It was told some of it.
act.moment: A council table with the captain standing rather than sitting, and one councillor's hand flat on the accounts.

current.name: Keep Above the Cloister
current.flavor: The keep took the height. The cloister was told the height was shared.

voice.name: Lieutenant's report, countersigned
voice.flavor: The chaplain countersigns, because the lieutenant's word alone is not worth the money it claims.
voice.moment: The chaplain's signature going under the lieutenant's on the same line, in a smaller hand.

cast.name: The Commission Above the Court
cast.reading: The legate stood on the step, so that the seal was higher than the finding.
cast.moment: The legate one step up holding the seal at eye level; the judge below him has not looked up yet.

act.line: The Watch on the Belfry, 26 April
act.detail: Everything the town knew that week it knew from men standing on the belfry counting fires.
act.moment: Two watchers counting enemy fires at dusk while a third writes the number down.

current.name: Office Above, Keep Beside
current.flavor: The office had the rise and the keep had the road, and both called it defence.

voice.name: Guard detail, three men, night watch
voice.flavor: One in three awake. The roll does not record which.
voice.moment: Three men at a brazier at night: one standing, and two who are not.

cast.name: The Judge Above the Gate
cast.reading: He read the writ from the gatehouse, because the yard was not safe and the writ still had to be read.
cast.moment: Reading aloud from a gate window into a courtyard where only two men are listening.

act.detail: The relief was expected and the gate stayed shut, because a gate opened for the wrong reason loses a town.
act.moment: The gatekeeper's hand on the bar and the captain beside him, both looking through the wicket at the road.

current.name: Keep Above, Office Beside
current.flavor: Stone above and office beside, in the order the bishop had agreed to.

voice.name: Materials, entered against the wrong account
voice.flavor: Sixty cartloads of stone charged to victuals. Corrected in a later hand, in a different ink.
voice.moment: Two entries on a page, the second written over the first in darker ink.

cast.name: The Seal Above, the Law Beside
cast.reading: They agreed the order of precedence in writing, which took longer than the case did.
cast.moment: Two men signing a short document while a third holds the inkhorn and says nothing.

act.detail: The wall was mended with stone from the houses of men standing there watching it.
act.moment: A mason setting a carved doorframe into a rampart while its owner watches from the crowd.

current.name: Office Above the Rampart
current.flavor: The office stood on the rampart and read to the men repairing it.

voice.name: Wages, short by four days
voice.flavor: The Exchequer allowed forty days and the campaign took forty-four. The four are still owed.
voice.moment: A man at the pay table counting the coins a second time while the clerk looks elsewhere.

cast.name: The Reading on the Rampart
cast.reading: He read the ordinance to the men repairing the wall, because they were the men it bound.
cast.moment: The judge on the wall-walk with the roll; below him a labourer has stopped with a stone in his hands.

act.detail: Published on the day the relief arrived, for reasons everyone understood.
act.moment: The proclamation being nailed to a post as the first relief carts come through behind it.

current.name: Rampart at the Bend
current.flavor: They walled the bend, which is where the road could be lost.

voice.name: Pioneers, hired by the day
voice.flavor: Not soldiers. Paid 4d, fed twice, and named individually because the town insisted.
voice.moment: A day-labourer's name written out in full, slowly, in a roll of abbreviations.

cast.name: The Barrier at the Turn
cast.reading: They walled the bend, because a bend is where a road stops being visible.
cast.moment: The last basket of earth going onto a new barricade at a corner, the road beyond it still empty.

act.detail: Built at the turn of the bridge, where neither side could see along the other's approach.
act.moment: A man straightening up from the work to look at what he still cannot see.

current.name: Corner Crusade
current.flavor: They set out from a corner and never rounded the second one.

voice.name: One lance, understrength, attested
voice.flavor: Man-at-arms, chaplain, archer — entered as a lance because the pay clerk allows it.
voice.moment: Three men standing close together while one bracket is drawn round three names.

cast.name: The Small Crusade
cast.reading: A knight, a judge and a labourer set out to do something about it. Cessolis would call that a complete society.
cast.moment: Three men leaving a yard at first light: one mounted, one on foot, one still fastening a bundle.

act.detail: Fifty went out at the Renart gate to burn a shed. It was the whole of the war news that week.
act.moment: The shed catching at one corner while the party is already turning back, none of them watching it burn.

current.name: Censer at the Turn
current.flavor: The censer swung at the turning and the smoke went the other way.

voice.name: Chaplain's fee, per sortie
voice.flavor: Sixpence a blessing, entered as 'divers necessaries'. Nine sorties that month.
voice.moment: A short column of identical sixpence entries running down a page.

cast.name: The Blessing at the Corner
cast.reading: The blessing was given at the turning, because after the turning nobody could see them from the town.
cast.moment: The censer at the top of its swing, and the rider beyond it already moving.

act.line: The Blessing at the Renart Gate, 4 January
act.detail: Every sortie was blessed at the gate. The blessing took less time than opening the gate.
act.moment: The gate half-open, the priest's hand still raised, the first horse's head already through.

current.name: Rider Above the Office
current.flavor: The rider took the high side. The office was told it was for safety.

voice.name: Escort, one day, disputed
voice.flavor: The chaplain says he was left. The man-at-arms says he rode ahead to look. Both are paid.
voice.moment: Two accounts of the same day written in the same book, half a page apart.

cast.name: The Horse on the High Side
cast.reading: The rider took the high ground, and the judge was told it was for his protection.
cast.moment: The rider on the bank above and the judge below on the track, both stopped, neither speaking.

act.line: The Escort to the Water Gate, 8 January
act.detail: The clergy went to bless the river gate. The escort chose the route and did not explain it.
act.moment: The escort turning his horse across the head of the path to stop the party going further.

current.name: The Guarded Homily
current.flavor: The homily was guarded. Nobody could say from what.

voice.name: One archer, detached, church duty
voice.flavor: Detached from the company for eight days. Complained. Detached for eight more.
voice.moment: One archer alone at a church door, bow unstrung, in the rain.

cast.name: The Guarded Reading
cast.reading: The reading was guarded. Nobody could say from what, only that it had been ordered.
cast.moment: A knight with his back to the lectern, facing an empty yard, while the reading goes on behind him.

act.detail: Preached under guard, in a church half outside the walls, to a congregation of forty.
act.moment: The doors held open by two soldiers looking outward while the congregation faces the other way.

current.name: Office and Outrider
current.flavor: The office kept the record; the outrider kept the pace.

voice.name: Reconnaissance, two men, one day
voice.flavor: Charged at 18d. The resulting sketch is bound into the account and is the best thing in it.
voice.moment: A rough map being pinned into a ledger with a knife.

cast.name: The Record and the Pace
cast.reading: The judge kept the record and the knight kept the pace, and the record fell behind.
cast.moment: The clerk half-running to keep up, writing on a board as he goes, the rider ahead not slowing.

act.line: The Count of the Bastilles, 15 January
act.detail: A rider and a clerk went round the outside of the town at a distance and counted.
act.moment: The clerk sketching the ring of forts onto a board while the rider watches the treeline behind him.

current.name: Lance Over Lectern
current.flavor: The lance stood over the lectern, and the reading continued.

voice.name: Divine service, attendance enforced
voice.flavor: The captain ordered it, the chaplain recorded it, and the archers stood at the back with their bows.
voice.moment: Armed men along the back wall of a church during a service, facing the congregation.

cast.name: The Lance Over the Lectern
cast.reading: The reading continued, because stopping it would have meant agreeing that it could be stopped.
cast.moment: The rider's lance across the corner of the frame, and below it a man reading on without looking up.

act.detail: Armed men came in during the office, and the office was finished anyway.
act.moment: Armed men entering at the back of a church, and the reader at the front not lifting his eyes from the page.

current.name: Two Lances at the Bend
current.flavor: Two lances at the bend, and the bend still went where it went.

voice.name: Two men-at-arms, one page: a lance
voice.flavor: Complete. The only complete lance on this page of the roll.
voice.moment: Three men and two horses standing in the one arrangement the clerk has a word for.

cast.name: Two Lances and a Boy
cast.reading: Two chevaliers and one pawn. Cessolis would say the pawn is the reason for the other two.
cast.moment: Two riders halted at a corner with a boy between the horses, holding both bridles.

act.detail: Two captains and a herdsman went out for beef. Only the beef was the point.
act.moment: Two riders driving a handful of cattle through a gap while a boy runs to keep them together.

current.name: The Cornered Pair
current.flavor: Cornered by the road, not by anyone following.

voice.name: Horse lost, not in action
voice.flavor: Drowned at a ford. The crown owes forty livres and will dispute it for two years.
voice.moment: A clerk writing a valuation while a wet saddle is carried past behind him.

cast.name: Cornered by the Road
cast.reading: They were not being followed. The road simply ran out, which is a different kind of trap.
cast.moment: Two riders and a boy stopped where a track ends at a flooded field, all three looking at the water.

act.detail: The winter river took the crossing, and the patrol found out at the crossing.
act.moment: A horse's forelegs in the water and the rider leaning back, the second rider already turning.

current.name: Riders on Two Sides
current.flavor: A rider on each side of the turning, and one boy between them.

voice.name: Escort of victuals, per journey
voice.flavor: Twelve journeys in January. The eleventh is marked 'lost' with no further note.
voice.moment: A line of twelve entries with the eleventh scored through.

cast.name: A Rider on Each Side
cast.reading: One knight each side of the turning and one boy between them, which is the whole arrangement of the world.
cast.moment: A boy walking up the middle of a lane with a mounted man either side, none of the three talking.

act.line: The Escort of the Miller, 25 January
act.detail: The mill outside the wall still worked, and the flour needed two horsemen to reach the gate.
act.moment: A sack of flour on a boy's shoulder between two riders, the gate still a hundred paces off.

current.name: Lance Beside the Keep
current.flavor: The horse waited beside the keep for a gate that opened late.

voice.name: Waiting time, claimed
voice.flavor: Four hours at a gate, claimed as service. Allowed, grudgingly, in a later hand.
voice.moment: A claim written in one hand and allowed in another underneath it.

cast.name: Waiting on the Gate
cast.reading: The legate's authority opened the gate. It did not say when.
cast.moment: A mounted man waiting at a closed gate with the seal already handed in, and nothing happening.

act.line: The Gate That Opened Late, 28 April
act.detail: The relief was outside from four o'clock. The gate opened at eight, when it was dark enough.
act.moment: Riders waiting in the dark under the wall, the first crack of light appearing at the gate's edge.

current.name: Keep Above the Lance
current.flavor: The keep held the height and the horse held the road beneath it.

voice.name: Signals, one man, standing duty
voice.flavor: Paid as an archer to stand still, which he says is harder.
voice.moment: One man alone on a high wall with a furled flag under his arm, looking at nothing yet.

cast.name: The Seal Above the Sworn
cast.reading: The commission held the height and the knight held the road, and both were following one order.
cast.moment: A man on a rampart holding up a sealed paper, and below him a rider reading it from the saddle.

act.line: The Signal from the Tower, 29 April
act.detail: The tower could see the convoy before the gate could. That was the whole value of the tower.
act.moment: A watcher with both arms up, and a rider below already wheeling his horse.

current.name: Lance Above, Keep Beside
current.flavor: The rider took the rise and the keep took the corner.

voice.name: Livestock, received into the town
voice.flavor: Counted twice, once at the gate and once in the market. The counts differ by nine.
voice.moment: Two tally sticks laid side by side on a table and not matching.

cast.name: The Rise and the Road
cast.reading: The rider took the rise, the legate took the corner, and the labourer was told to stand in the middle.
cast.moment: Three men on three levels of the same broken ground, none of them looking at each other.

act.detail: Six hundred head came in from the south while the English watched from Saint-Privé and did nothing.
act.moment: Cattle streaming through a gate under the eyes of a distant fort, a rider counting them as they pass.

current.name: Keep Above, Lance Beside
current.flavor: Stone on the height, horse at its foot, and the road watched twice.

voice.name: Boats, hired, with their men
voice.flavor: Eleven boats and their crews, paid by the boat and not the man. The men noticed.
voice.moment: A boatman paid one coin for four men, all four watching his hand.

cast.name: Watched Twice
cast.reading: Stone on the height, horse at its foot: one road watched by two men who did not speak.
cast.moment: A rider at the base of a tower and a watcher at the top, both facing the same empty road.

act.detail: The convoy came round by the east bank, because the west bank was watched.
act.moment: Loaded boats poled upriver at dusk with a rider keeping pace along the bank.

current.name: Lance Above the Rampart
current.flavor: The rider crossed above the rampart while it was still being built.

voice.name: Work under fire, extra allowance
voice.flavor: Twopence a day above the rate, claimed by everyone within a mile of it.
voice.moment: A long list of claimants for a twopenny allowance, in several hands.

cast.name: Crossing the Unfinished Wall
cast.reading: He rode over the rampart while it was still being built, which is how you learn it is not a wall yet.
cast.moment: A horse picking its way across a half-built rampart while the men building it stand back.

act.detail: They fortified the ruin of the fort they had taken, working under fire from the next one along.
act.moment: Men working with their heads down while a rider crosses the gap behind them at speed.

current.name: Sally from the Bend
current.flavor: They came out at the bend, where the road could not be seen along.

voice.name: Sortie pay, one day, double
voice.flavor: Double rate for the day of a sortie. The roll for 3 May is the longest in the book.
voice.moment: A single day's page carrying three times the names of the pages either side of it.

cast.name: The Sally at the Blind Corner
cast.reading: They came out at the bend, because a bend is the only place a wall can surprise anybody.
cast.moment: The gate at the bend swinging in and the first horse coming out, the road beyond still empty.

act.line: The Sortie from the Burgundy Gate, 3 May
act.detail: They went out where the wall turns, so that the bastille could not see the gate open.
act.moment: The postern at the angle of the wall standing open with men already fifty paces beyond it.

current.name: Corner Chapel
current.flavor: They built the corner first. The rest of the chapel never came.

voice.name: Two labourers and a chaplain
voice.flavor: The chaplain certifies the stone came from consecrated ground and may be reused.
voice.moment: A chalk mark going onto a stone before it is loaded, the chaplain's hand steadying it.

cast.name: The Corner Built First
cast.reading: They built the corner first, because a corner is two walls. The rest never came.
cast.moment: Two labourers setting the last stone of a corner that stands alone in a field, the judge watching.

act.detail: Another suburb church came down. The stone went into the wall, which the canons had agreed to.
act.moment: A church corner dismantled stone by stone, a cleric marking each one with chalk.

current.name: The Curate's Corner
current.flavor: The curate took the inside of the bend, where the wind was smaller.

voice.name: Travel allowance, three men, winter rate
voice.flavor: A penny a day extra from Martinmas. The clerk has written the date of the change in the margin.
voice.moment: A margin note giving a date, with the rate above it changing on that line.

cast.name: The Inside of the Bend
cast.reading: The curate took the inside of the bend, where the wind was smaller, and nobody begrudged him it.
cast.moment: Three figures walking a bend, the cleric on the sheltered side, the two labourers taking the weather.

act.line: The Winter Road to Blois, 6 November
act.detail: The last road still open, and the wind on it came straight off the river.
act.moment: Three figures leaning into wind on an embankment, the middle one shielded by the other two.

current.name: Vespers at the Bend
current.flavor: Vespers was said at the turning. Nobody agreed on the hour.

voice.name: Locked out, one night, no allowance
voice.flavor: Arrived after the gate closed. Not the town's problem, and not the crown's.
voice.moment: Three men sleeping against the outside of a town wall, gear stacked between them.

cast.name: Vespers on the Road
cast.reading: The hour was said on the road, because they would not reach the town before it.
cast.moment: Three men stopped on a road at dusk: one reading, two standing with their loads still on.

act.detail: Said in the open by men who could not get in before the gate closed. The gate did not open for it.
act.moment: Three figures kneeling on open ground with a shut gate behind them and one light in it.

current.name: The Bend Patrol
current.flavor: They patrolled the bend because the straight road no longer mattered.

voice.name: Standing patrol, three men, nightly
voice.flavor: Entered once with 'and so on nightly', which the Exchequer disallowed.
voice.moment: A single roll entry with a long horizontal stroke drawn after it.

cast.name: The Patrol of the Turning
cast.reading: They patrolled the bend, because the straight road no longer mattered to anybody.
cast.moment: A rider and two men on foot at a corner, all three looking down a road nobody uses.

act.line: The Watch on the Portereau, 12 November
act.detail: The English were building. The town's task that month was to watch them do it and write it down.
act.moment: Two men and a rider on a bank watching earthworks go up half a mile away.

current.name: Rider at the Elbow
current.flavor: The horse held the elbow of the road, and the road held nothing else.

voice.name: Post, three men, held eleven days
voice.flavor: Relieved on the twelfth. Two of the three were the same two throughout.
voice.moment: Two men handing a post over to two others, one of the four already walking away.

cast.name: The Elbow of the Road
cast.reading: The horse held the elbow of the road, and the road held nothing else.
cast.moment: A mounted man in the crook of a bend with a man on foot either side, all three still.

act.detail: The last open track east, held by three men because there were not four to spare.
act.moment: Three men at a junction in the rain with a hurdle half across it.

current.name: Last Horse in the Lane
current.flavor: One horse remained in the lane. The lane remembered more.

voice.name: One horse remaining, appraised
voice.flavor: Of eleven horses entered in October, one is still standing in November's roll.
voice.moment: A page with ten valuations struck through and one left.

cast.name: The Last Horse
cast.reading: One horse remained in the lane. The lane remembered more of them than that.
cast.moment: One rider and two men on foot in a lane wide enough for a column, with nothing else in it.

act.detail: The town began to count its horses as food in November, and the counting was done in public.
act.moment: A horse led past a queue of people who are all looking at it and not at each other.

current.name: Three at the Turning
current.flavor: The road bent. Three of them bent with it, and did not straighten.

voice.name: Three foot archers, one street
voice.flavor: Entered in the order the street runs, which is how the whole roll is arranged.
voice.moment: Three names one under another with a street name bracketing all three.

cast.name: The Labourer, the Smith and the Taverner
cast.reading: First, second and sixth pawn: the spade, the hammer and the cup. The array took all three in a morning.
cast.moment: Three men handing their tools over a fence to somebody out of frame, one after another.

act.line: The Levy at the Turning, 13 October
act.detail: Three off one street. The names were read at the corner where the street bends.
act.moment: Three men stepping out of a doorway into a lane while a clerk reads from a list at the corner.

current.name: The Corner Tower
current.flavor: The corner tower saw two roads and reported neither.

voice.name: Watch, two men, one tower, alternating
voice.flavor: Six hours each. The relief is recorded; the sleep is not.
voice.moment: Two men passing on a narrow stair, one going up, one coming down.

cast.name: The Tower on the Corner
cast.reading: The corner tower saw two roads and reported neither, because reporting was not in the commission.
cast.moment: A man at a tower window with two roads visible below him and no paper in his hands.

act.detail: Two roads visible from the belfry and one watcher, who could only be looking at one of them.
act.moment: A watcher turning from one window to another in a bell chamber, the bell rope hanging still.

current.name: Tower Above the Lane
current.flavor: The tower stood above the lane after the lane stopped being used.

voice.name: Rubble, carted, sixty loads
voice.flavor: Charged by the load. The loads got smaller as the month went on.
voice.moment: Two tally marks of different sizes cut on the same stick.

cast.name: Above the Disused Lane
cast.reading: The tower stood above the lane after the lane stopped being used, and went on standing above it.
cast.moment: Two men below a tower clearing a lane that plainly nobody has walked down in months.

act.detail: They filled the lane with rubble, because it ran to a gate they no longer meant to open.
act.moment: Two men tipping a barrow of rubble into a lane while a third watches from above.

current.name: Keep at the Turning
current.flavor: The keep held the turning. The turning was all it held.

voice.name: Garrison, three men, thirty-one days
voice.flavor: Nothing occurred. The roll still runs to a page, because the pay does.
voice.moment: A full page of identical daily entries.

cast.name: The Turning Was All It Held
cast.reading: The keep held the turning. Held is a generous word for what a building does.
cast.moment: Two men and an officer at a gatehouse on a bend, none of them doing anything.

act.line: The Post at the Bend, 14 January
act.detail: A gatehouse at a turn in the wall, three men, and a month with nothing in it.
act.moment: Three men in a gatehouse arch, one asleep sitting up, the road empty in both directions.

current.name: Traveling Chapel
current.flavor: The chapel traveled because the wounded could not.

voice.name: Two chaplains, two servants, one cart
voice.flavor: The cart is charged to the retinue. Everything in it is charged to the town.
voice.moment: A loaded cart with two men roping it and two clerics counting what is on it.

cast.name: The Portable Court
cast.reading: Two judges, two clerks, and everything the office needs in one cart, because the office has lost its room.
cast.moment: A cart being packed with a table, a chest and a folded cloth; one judge is already sitting in it.

act.detail: The wounded from Rouvray came back over two days and were put wherever there was floor.
act.moment: Two clerics laying a man on straw in a room already full, two townsmen carrying in the next one.

current.name: Chapel Corner to Corner
current.flavor: Two offices, opposite corners, and the same short liturgy between them.

voice.name: Divided company, two stations
voice.flavor: Half at the bridge, half at the north gate. One roll, two pay tables, endless argument.
voice.moment: Two pay tables in one room with a queue at each and a clerk shouting across.

cast.name: Two Courts, One Square
cast.reading: Two judges at opposite corners of one yard, each hearing his own case, each audible to the other.
cast.moment: A small yard with a table in each of two corners and one man crossing between them.

act.detail: Two chapels at opposite ends of the town kept the vigil for the dead of Rouvray, an hour apart.
act.moment: A lit doorway at each end of a dark street with one figure walking from one to the other.

current.name: Wayfarers' Compact
current.flavor: They agreed upon the road, having nowhere left to meet.

voice.name: Composite lance, four men, four rates
voice.flavor: Man-at-arms 12d, chaplain 6d, two archers 6d. Four men, three arguments.
voice.moment: Four different coin counts made onto the same table in front of four men.

cast.name: The Compact on the Road
cast.reading: Four men who would not have met agreed how to travel together, because none of them could travel alone.
cast.moment: Four men shaking on it at a crossroads, the horse already turned toward one of the four roads.

act.detail: Scots on foot, French on horse, and an argument about who went first that lost the battle.
act.moment: Four men arguing over a line scratched in the dirt while the English carts are visible behind them.

current.name: Office Above, Horse Beside
current.flavor: The office kept the height; the horse kept the exit.

voice.name: Position, disputed in the account
voice.flavor: The chaplain's account and the man-at-arms' account of the same field do not agree.
voice.moment: Two written accounts pinned side by side, one annotated in a third hand.

cast.name: The Office Above, the Horse Beside
cast.reading: The judge took the height and the knight took the exit, and the two labourers took what was left.
cast.moment: Four men on broken ground — one high, one at the gap, two in the low middle — each watching something different.

act.detail: The French had the height and the horse and lost anyway, which took a long time to explain.
act.moment: Four men on a rise looking down at the wagon-fort, one of them pointing at the wrong part of it.

current.name: Compact of the Square
current.flavor: Four corners, one agreement, and nothing to enforce it.

voice.name: Four names, one indenture, no seal
voice.flavor: Agreed and never sealed. Paid anyway, which is how most of it worked.
voice.moment: An unsealed document with four signatures and a blank wax disc beside it.

cast.name: Four Corners, One Agreement
cast.reading: They agreed it in a square yard with a man at each corner, so that nobody could be overheard.
cast.moment: Four men at four corners of a yard, all facing inward, none close enough to touch.

act.detail: The town, the church, the garrison and the crown met about the grain. Nothing was enforceable.
act.moment: Four men round a table with the grain accounts in the middle and nobody's hand on them.

current.name: Escort of Lances
current.flavor: Four riders escorted linen farther than any standard.

voice.name: Two lances, forty days, victual escort
voice.flavor: Retained to bring the carts in. Paid whether the carts arrive or not, which was foreseen.
voice.moment: Two mounted men counted past a clerk at a road barrier, carts stacked behind them.

cast.name: The Escort of the Merchant
cast.reading: Fourth pawn is the merchant, who carries the scales. Two knights were hired to walk beside them.
cast.moment: Two riders halted while the merchant reweighs a sack at the roadside, the fourth man holding the horses.

act.detail: Three hundred carts of salt fish for Lent, and an escort under orders not to fight for them.
act.moment: Two riders alongside a cart of barrels at the instant the commander's hand goes up to halt the column.

current.name: Lances at Opposite Corners
current.flavor: Two lances at opposite corners, watching the same empty middle.

voice.name: Front and rear guard, same rate
voice.flavor: Two men-at-arms, one at each end, entered on the first and the last line of the page.
voice.moment: A page of the roll with a man-at-arms' name at the very top and another at the very bottom.

cast.name: A Lance at Each End
cast.reading: One knight at the head and one at the tail, and the two men between them could not see either.
cast.moment: A sunken lane: a rider visible at the front, a rider visible at the back, and nothing else.

act.detail: The escort was strung along a mile of road when the attack came at the middle of it.
act.moment: The middle of a column — two carters looking forward and back in the same instant, both riders too far away.

current.name: Blessing of the Square
current.flavor: He blessed all four corners. Three had already been abandoned.

voice.name: One chaplain, three archers, parish duty
voice.flavor: Detailed to the parish for the octave. Returned two men short, both accounted for.
voice.moment: Four men leaving and two coming back, past the same clerk at the same gate.

cast.name: The Blessing of the Four Corners
cast.reading: He blessed all four corners of the yard. Three of the four houses on it were already empty.
cast.moment: A cleric at the fourth corner with three labourers behind him, looking at three shuttered doors.

act.line: The Blessing of the Quarters, 21 December
act.detail: Each quarter was blessed before Christmas. Two of them had nobody left in them to hear it.
act.moment: A small procession turning into an empty street, the leading cleric's hand raised at nothing.

current.name: Rider in the Square
current.flavor: The seal was unbroken. The stable boy had already understood.

voice.name: Messenger, mounted, three attendants
voice.flavor: Three men to see one letter safely twelve miles. It arrived.
voice.moment: One sealed letter on an open palm, three sets of hands near it and none of them touching it.

cast.name: The Sealed Letter
cast.reading: The seal was unbroken when it reached him. The boy who carried it had already understood what was in it.
cast.moment: A rider taking a sealed letter from a boy who does not let go of it immediately.

act.line: The News of Salisbury's Death, 5 November
act.detail: It took three days to be believed, and the believing changed nothing about the walls.
act.moment: A letter handed over in a courtyard where three men have stopped work to watch.

current.name: The Fourfold Yoke
current.flavor: Four to a yoke meant for oxen. The oxen had been eaten in spring.

voice.name: Four foot archers, employed as haulage
voice.flavor: Paid 3d, worked as beasts, and the clerk has written 'as oxen' with no evident irony.
voice.moment: Four names bracketed under a heading in the clerk's hand reading 'as oxen'.

cast.name: Four to the Yoke
cast.reading: Labourer, smith, taverner, guard: four estates, one yoke, and the oxen eaten in spring.
cast.moment: Four men taking the weight of a cart-yoke meant for animals, at the instant it comes off the ground.

act.detail: Everything outside the walls that could be moved was moved in one day, by hand, because there were no beasts.
act.moment: Four men dragging a loaded cart through a gate too narrow for it, one of them turned sideways.

current.name: Rampart Detail
current.flavor: They repaired the wall with stones from the abandoned quarter.

voice.name: Masonry, three men and an overseer
voice.flavor: Materials 'found on site', which is the clerk's phrase for taken.
voice.moment: A ledger line reading 'found on site', with a loaded barrow visible through a doorway.

cast.name: The Repair Detail
cast.reading: The legate's commission covered the wall. It did not cover where the stone came from.
cast.moment: Three men lifting a dressed stone with a carved face on it into a rough wall, while an officer looks away.

act.line: The Wall Repaired with the Quarter, 20 February
act.detail: They mended the rampart with the stone of the abandoned quarter, and the owners helped.
act.moment: A carved lintel going into a rampart, held level by three men, its carving still facing out.
